title: StrongReject Score Distribution Across Attack Strategies: Which Attacks Produce the Highest-Quality Harmful Content?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quality-weighted attack comparison is more informative than binary ASR for actual capability uplift risk. Directly informs threat modeling by distinguishing truly dangerous attacks from ones that produce vague harmful content.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running 5 different attack types, which means setting up multiple attack pipelines (GCG, prefilling, roleplay, multi-turn, multilingual). The StrongReject evaluator is public, but the multi-attack setup is complex for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Five attack types times 40 prompts, each requiring different setup (GCG optimization, multi-turn conversation loops, translation). The breadth of attack implementations makes this too wide for 30 hours.
